extracted.intended_audience: energy regulators, compliance officers at utilities and Regional Entities, energy lawyers, FERC/NERC staff, and energy law scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the evaluative standards and procedural requirements FERC has imposed on NERC and Regional Entities for implementing risk‑based compliance and enforcement programs (FFT, RAI, compliance exceptions, self‑logging, audits, transparency, and metrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation necessary for auditable demonstration of compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation is necessary to establish a reasonably auditable demonstration of compliance and may reinforce focus on attaining the performance required by a Reliability Standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC and NERC emphasize creating records adequate to support findings of violations; streamlined formats must still permit an auditable record. Anti-pattern: eliminating documentation that prevents auditing or verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear criteria for FFT eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be clear criteria for FFT (Find, Fix, Track, and Report) eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC conditioned acceptance of FFTs on explicit eligibility criteria so that only appropriate minimal (and in some limited cases, specified moderate) risk matters receive FFT processing. Programs must document the eligibility rules and apply them consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency through public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: NERC and Regional Entities must maintain transparency through public posting of FFTs and other abbreviated submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC repeatedly required public posting (e.g., monthly FFT spreadsheets on NERC’s website) and denied proposals to eliminate public postings of compliance exceptions or self‑logged items. Transparency educates industry and provides oversight; anti-pattern: removing public posting to 'avoid diverting attention.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The mitigation of violations must be verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC required that when violations are submitted as FFTs or other abbreviated formats, the claimed mitigation must be confirmed. Unverified mitigation is insufficient for streamlined dispositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in implementation across Regional Entities
rubrics_metrics.description: NERC must demonstrate consistent implementation of programs (FFT, RAI, compliance exceptions, etc.) across the various Regional Entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC repeatedly required NERC to show that Regional Entities apply qualifications, documentation, accountability, and deterrence uniformly (unless regional facts require a difference). Annual reports must assess Regional Entity consistency; inconsistent regional application is a core concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk‑based treatment focused on higher‑risk issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance monitoring and enforcement should focus time and effort on higher‑risk issues while still identifying, correcting, and tracking lesser‑risk issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC’s risk‑based programs (FFT, RAI) are intended to direct resources toward greater reliability risks; however, efficiencies must not compromise oversight or visibility of all noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined documentation and expedited processing for minimal risk
rubrics_metrics.description: For minimal‑risk violations, programs may use streamlined documentation formats and expedited resolution to reduce paperwork and speed processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC accepted streamlined formats (e.g., FFT spreadsheets, SNOPs) for minimal‑risk matters but tied acceptance to other safeguards (verification, posting, sampling). Anti-pattern: streamlining without safeguards that preserve oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for evaluating an entity’s compliance history
rubrics_metrics.description: NERC must provide the principles it will employ in evaluating an entity’s compliance history when determining eligibility for streamlined treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC directed NERC to articulate how prior violations, including repeat or closely‑related noncompliance, inform decisions about FFT or compliance exception treatment; this includes assessing whether to continue exception treatment after subsequent noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for deciding FFT treatment during monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional Entity compliance staff must have articulated procedures for how they will decide whether FFT treatment is appropriate during compliance monitoring activities (e.g., audits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC required NERC to explain how staff will make case‑by‑case determinations, including use of inherent risk assessments and scoping based on entity‑specific risk factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting cadence and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: FFT spreadsheets and similar abbreviated reports should be publicly posted (NERC posts monthly) and may use spreadsheet formats that briefly describe each violation and mitigation activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC approved monthly public posting of FFTs and permitted Regional Entities to post on the last day of each month in lieu of separate monthly filings. Posts must be sufficiently informative to allow oversight and sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative sampling and review of FFTs/compliance exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: FERC requires review of a representative sample of FFTs and compliance exceptions (e.g., within a 60‑day window after posting and/or annual random sampling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling provides oversight of streamlined dispositions; FERC has directed staff or NERC to conduct surveys/sampling to evaluate program performance and consistent implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on expansion of streamlined treatment to moderate risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Expansion of FFT or compliance exception treatment to moderate‑risk violations is allowed only in limited, specified circumstances and subject to reporting and review commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC approved limited extensions (e.g., some moderate risk possible violations subject to reporting) but explicitly rejected broader proposals to treat moderate risks as minimal without safeguards. Proposals expanding scope must include robust data and oversight assurances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of compliance exceptions (no elimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance exceptions identified through self‑logging or other means must be publicly posted; proposals to eliminate such postings have been denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC found benefits in public posting (education, oversight) and rejected NERC’s argument that posting self‑logged trivial instances diverts attention from higher risk matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of repeat noncompliance when granting exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional Entities must assess any subsequent noncompliance of the same or closely‑related standards to determine whether an entity should continue to qualify for compliance exception treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC conditioned approval of compliance exceptions on Regional Entity review of recurrence/risk of repeated noncompliance; persistence of related noncompliance can remove eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal review of internal controls before self‑logging flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Before granting entities the flexibility to self‑log instances of noncompliance, there must be some level of formal review of the entity’s internal controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC found it unreasonable to allow self‑logging without formal verification that the entity’s controls are effective; self‑logging eligibility should be limited to entities with demonstrated effective management practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria and presumption for self‑logging
rubrics_metrics.description: Self‑logging is intended for registered entities with demonstrated effective management practices; properly logged items are presumed resolved as compliance exceptions unless additional risk factors exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC proposed a presumption in favor of compliance exceptions for self‑logged items, but FERC insists on controls review, reporting, and visibility to prevent misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: NERC Rules of Procedure must articulate RAI concepts and elements
rubrics_metrics.description: NERC’s Rules of Procedure must recognize RAI processes, articulate basic RAI concepts, define fundamental RAI elements (compliance exceptions, self‑logging, internal controls evaluations, etc.), and require Commission approval for significant changes in RAI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC required explicit Rule of Procedure language because existing rules were inadequate to authorize the RAI framework. Rules must also explain types of data used to identify risk elements and monitoring approaches tied to entity risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe data types and monitoring tool selection in Rules of Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules should (1) highlight the types of data NERC uses to identify annual risk elements and (2) explain that the type and frequency of compliance monitoring tools are based on an entity’s specific reliability risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC directed NERC to make transparent how data informs risk prioritization and monitoring choices; guidance helps ensure consistent, defendable scoping decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop success factors and data‑driven metrics for RAI
rubrics_metrics.description: NERC must develop success factors and data‑driven metrics enabling NERC and FERC to evaluate the success of RAI, including: (1) a thorough analysis of lessons learned; (2) metrics showing how the risk‑based approach enhanced reliability; and (3) metrics showing improvements such as faster detection and remediation times for minor violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC repeatedly required measurable metrics (not just violation counts) tied to reliability outcomes; proposals without adequate metrics were conditionally accepted or rejected. Metrics should support iterative program evaluation and the feedback loop to standards development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie performance metrics to standards development (feedback loop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common performance measures should be tied to ongoing reliability standards development to create a feedback loop where enforcement informs standards revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC encouraged NERC to link enforcement metrics to standards improvement so noncompliance patterns can identify needed standard changes; this strengthens results‑based reliability standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reporting of all noncompliance to NERC and FERC
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional Entities must continue to report all noncompliance to NERC and FERC, preserving visibility into every violation (including those in abbreviated formats or self‑logged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC rejected proposals that would remove reporting or reduce visibility. Prompt reporting is required per regulations (e.g., 18 C.F.R. § 39.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum audit periodicity and rigorous audits for core entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum periodicity of audits for reliability coordinators, balancing authorities, and transmission operators should be maintained; rigorous audits of compliance cannot be eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC denied proposals to remove minimum audit periods and found such removals inconsistent with the need for rigorous, periodic evidence reviews. Audit frequency and scope should be risk‑informed but not permissive to the point of eroding oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence retention and timely reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for evidence retention and timely reporting of violations must be preserved; reductions that erode oversight are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC cited concerns over proposed reductions in evidence retention and lack of set audit periods as exacerbating oversight risks. Programs must ensure sufficient records for reviews and audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform regional processes unless justified by regional facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional processes should be uniform unless regional facts (other than custom) justify differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC emphasized uniformity across Regional Entities to avoid inconsistent reliability outcomes; deviations must be justified by objective regional differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic assessment of Regional Entities’ consistency in annual reports
rubrics_metrics.description: NERC must provide assessments of the Regional Entities’ consistency in implementing risk‑based compliance and enforcement in its annual reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC directed NERC to include evaluations of consistency and to tie reported metrics to program improvements and oversight findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use meaningful reliability indicators beyond violation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance measurement should move beyond simple violation counts to meaningful indicators of reliability improvement (e.g., detection/remediation speed, thematic trends, lessons learned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC called for data‑driven metrics that demonstrate that efficiency gains correlate with enhanced reliability outcomes rather than merely reduced administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance efficiency gains with retention of meaningful oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Any efficiency or streamlining proposal must preserve meaningful Commission and NERC oversight and transparency; efficiency alone is not sufficient justification to reduce visibility and oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERC repeatedly approved efficiency measures conditionally and rejected proposals that would 'remove from [FERC] review much of the ERO’s enforcement of Reliability Standards.' Proposals should document how oversight will be preserved.
